source.title: Using Scaling Laws for Data Source Utility Estimation in Domain-Specific Pre-Training
source.authors: Oleksiy Ostapenko; Charles Guille-Escuret; Luke Kumar; Max Tian; Denis Kocetkov; Gopeshh Subbaraj; Raymond Li; J. Lamy-Poirier; Sébastien Paquet; Torsten Scholak

record.tranche_reason: The study estimates scaling curves in a new setting—domain-specific data-source utility during annealing—but does not test the listed model-loss, model-size, or compute-optimal allocation claims.
record.gate_note: The study reports data-source utility trends across annealing compute, not held-out pretraining loss as a function of model parameters, training tokens, or compute. Its curves and source-ranking results are recorded as related findings under fits_no_version. The mathematical and medical scoring prompts and WRAP prompt templates in the text are example task prompts, not instructions to an AI reviewing the paper.
record.test_reason: The study borrows the scaling-law idea as a tool. It fits log-linear curves of a data source's downstream utility (Brier Score delta against full replay) against curation and annealing FLOPs for one fixed 7B model. It reports no held-out pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute. It does not vary model size. Its downstream measure is a per-source gain relative to a replay baseline, not performance against model scale or pretraining loss. So no version (V1–V7) is tested; the findings are recorded under fits_no_version. The record's T3 conflicts with its own uses_without_test relation; T4 fits better.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that multiple annealing runs of varying compute yield per-source utility scaling curves, and that source rankings shift with scale (e.g., MBF improves while WRAP suffers diminishing returns). They add that data sources should be matched to the evaluation format and the available compute, not just the domain.
record.recipe_differences: Fits downstream data-source utility against curation and annealing compute for a fixed 7B model; it does not fit held-out pretraining loss against model size, training tokens, or training compute.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported source rankings vary with compute scale and evaluation format. The authors also state that WRAP results are more variable at low scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Medical MMLU CF: WRAP beats MBF at low compute, but WRAP shows diminishing returns and MBF keeps improving; the ranking reverses with compute.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Data-source utility rankings during annealing are not invariant across compute scales, so small-scale point estimates can mislead.

fits_no_version.finding: Math MMLU CF: TinyGSM is better at small budgets, while TinyGSM-MIND scales better overall.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The relative utility of synthetic data sources depends on annealing compute scale.

fits_no_version.finding: Log-linear utility fits vary widely in quality: R² 0.8–0.9 for MBF/WRAP (medical) and MIND (math), but 0.1–0.2 for math MBF and TinyGSM and 0.4 for Instr.Aug.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-source utility-vs-compute curves are fittable for some sources but noisy for others at a single seed.

record.problems: Experiments use one 7B model scale; the authors say they could not extend experiments to compute budgets orders of magnitude larger. Most non-baseline results use a single seed, and the authors note low-scale stochasticity and limited ablations. Scaling curves are shown in figures, with dotted portions extrapolated.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results were left out.

untested.parts: All: no pretraining loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
All: no model-loss extrapolation; the authors could not test runs orders of magnitude larger.
All: continued pretraining (annealing) utility curves are fitted, but not loss power laws in N, D or C.
All: downstream gains are shown against data-source compute for a fixed model, not against model scale or pretraining loss.

missing.what: Instruction augmentation utility curve (medical CF): it does not beat full replay on CF, but matches WRAP on MC; fit R² 0.4.
Fit R² values per source and per cost axis.
Exact-match gains on non-MMLU math tasks against FLOPs for MBF, TinyGSM and MIND.
Evaluation-format sensitivity: MC and generative scores swing with MMLU-style Q/A in the data, while CF stays stable.

record.verdict_notes: 'Scaling laws' here means utility-vs-data-compute curves for a fixed model (form Δ = a + b·log c), not Kaplan/Chinchilla loss laws. The study is not an original source. Single seed for non-baseline runs; the authors note low-scale stochasticity. rows_left_out ('none left out') is inaccurate given the Instr.Aug., Fig. 6 and Fig. 3 results.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from smaller-run model-loss fits.
Compute-optimal parameter and token allocation for training language models.
Effects of architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Scaling-law behavior in other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning, or transfer.
Predictability of downstream performance from model scale or pretraining loss.
Sensitivity of model-loss exponents or compute-optimal splits to model-training setup and fitting choices.
